title: Respond to a trademark office action
summary: An office action is a letter from the USPTO examiner, not a rejection of your company. It raises refusals (likelihood of confusion, descriptiveness) or requirements, and each needs an answer. You have three months from the issue date plus one paid three-month extension. Madrid Section 66(a) filings get six months and no extension (rule card us-fed.trademark-office-action-response, USPTO guidance cited). Miss the deadline and the application abandons. Pull the cited marks on TSDR. Decide: argue, amend, or hire counsel. File the signed response in TEAS. This is what happens when the filing from 'File trademark' comes back with questions. Educational guidance, not legal advice.

parts.title: Read the office action: substantive refusals (likelihood of confusion, descriptiveness) vs procedural requirements
Calendar the deadline: 3 months from the issue date, one 3-month paid extension (Madrid §66(a): 6 months, no extension)
Pull the examiner's cited marks on TSDR and check their live status
Decide the response: argue, amend the application, or bring in trademark counsel
Draft the response and its evidence
Sign and file the response in TEAS before the deadline
Wait for the examiner: approval, a final action, or new issues

metadata.trigger: The USPTO examiner issues an office action against your trademark application: refusals or requirements with a response deadline.
metadata.supportReason: Likelihood-of-confusion arguments are legal craft and the TEAS filing carries the applicant's or attorney's signature. An agent can pull the cited marks' TSDR records; the response is human work.

contextNeeded.query: the office action (serial number, issue date, refusal grounds)

geoNotes.summary: The UKIPO issues an examination report with a two-month response window — objections commonly on distinctiveness, plus notifications of earlier marks surfaced in the search (the UK notifies rather than refuses on relative grounds). Respond, amend, or let it lapse.

A DPMA Beanstandung names the defect (absolute grounds, classification, formalities) with its own stated response deadline; relative grounds arrive later as oppositions after publication — answer through the DPMA's procedures or counsel, inside the stated window.

INPI examination raises objections with the notification's own reply deadline, and third-party oppositions run on fixed windows after publication — both are answered through the INPI e-procedures portal, which is also where the file's status lives.

The registry's examination report must be answered within 30 days of receipt or the application is treated as abandoned — the report and the application status live on the registry's online search, and responses go through an agent or attorney.

INPI raises refusals and irregularities with its own stated response deadline, and published applications face a two-month opposition window — answer through INPI's online services, with counsel for substantive refusals.

A CIPO examiner's report names the objections (confusion, descriptiveness, formalities) with its own stated response deadline — answer every ground through CIPO's online channel or the application lapses.
